guide_line: Compare effusion rates with Graham's law.
steps: Diffusion is mixing as gas particles wander from a crowded place into a less crowded one. Effusion is escape through a tiny hole into a vacuum.
Graham: rate1/rate2 = sqrt(M2/M1). The lighter gas moves faster.
Time is the reverse of rate. The heavier gas takes longer by the factor sqrt(M_heavy/M_light).
In the same amount of time, distance follows the rate. The lighter gas travels farther.

worked_example.q: How many times faster does He effuse than N2? He is 4.0026 g/mol and N2 is 28.014 g/mol. Report the rate ratio rate(He)/rate(N2).
steps: He is lighter, so its rate is larger.

similar_problem.q: How many times faster does He effuse than O2? He is 4.0026 g/mol and O2 is 31.998 g/mol. Report rate(He)/rate(O2).
similar_problem.hint: Put 31.998 over 4.0026 inside a square root to get rate(He)/rate(O2).

problems.q: How many times faster does He effuse than Ar? He is 4.0026 g/mol and Ar is 39.948 g/mol. Report rate(He)/rate(Ar).
hints: rate(He)/rate(Ar) is the square root of 39.948/4.0026.

problems.q: How many times faster does N2 effuse than O2? N2 is 28.014 g/mol and O2 is 31.998 g/mol. Report rate(N2)/rate(O2).
hints: N2 is the lighter gas here. Square-root 31.998/28.014.

problems.q: How many times faster does H2 effuse than Cl2? H2 is 2.016 g/mol and Cl2 is 70.90 g/mol. Report rate(H2)/rate(Cl2).
hints: Square-root the mass ratio 70.90/2.016 to compare H2 with Cl2.

problems.q: Under the same conditions, He effuses in 12.50 s. How many seconds does O2 take? He is 4.0026 g/mol and O2 is 31.998 g/mol.
hints: O2 is heavier, so multiply the 12.50 s helium time by sqrt(31.998/4.0026).

problems.q: Under the same setup, an unknown gas effuses in 48.00 s and N2 effuses in 32.00 s. N2 is 28.014 g/mol. What is the molar mass of the unknown gas, in g/mol?
hints: The unknown is slower, so M = 28.014 × (48.00/32.00)^2.

problems.q: In the same time, He travels 40.00 cm. How far does Ne travel, in cm? He is 4.0026 g/mol and Ne is 20.180 g/mol.
hints: Ne is heavier, so multiply 40.00 cm by sqrt(4.0026/20.180).

problems.q: Which gas effuses faster, F2 or Ne? F2 is 37.996 g/mol and Ne is 20.180 g/mol. Type the formula.
problems.why: Ne has the smaller molar mass, so it effuses faster than F2.
hints: Ne is 20.180 g/mol and F2 is 37.996 g/mol. The lighter gas is faster, so type Ne.

problems.q: A gas effuses 3.159 times as fast as Ar. Ar is 39.948 g/mol. What is the molar mass of the unknown gas, in g/mol?
hints: Set 3.159 equal to sqrt(39.948/M). Square 3.159, then divide 39.948 by that square.

problems.q: In the same time, H2 travels 50.00 cm. How far does O2 travel, in cm? H2 is 2.016 g/mol and O2 is 31.998 g/mol.
hints: O2 is heavier than H2, so multiply 50.00 cm by sqrt(2.016/31.998).

problems.q: How many times faster does CH4 effuse than SO2? CH4 is 16.043 g/mol and SO2 is 64.058 g/mol. Report rate(CH4)/rate(SO2).
hints: Square-root 64.058/16.043 to get the methane-to-sulfur-dioxide rate ratio.

problems.q: A gas leaks through a pinhole into vacuum. Type the name of this process.
problems.why: Escape through a tiny hole into vacuum is effusion. Diffusion is mixing through open space.
hints: Leakage through a tiny hole into vacuum is called effusion. Type that one word.

problems.q: Which gas effuses faster, Cl2 or F2? Cl2 is 70.90 g/mol and F2 is 37.996 g/mol. Type the formula.
problems.why: F2 is lighter than Cl2, so F2 effuses faster.
hints: Compare 37.996 g/mol with 70.90 g/mol and type the lighter formula, F2.

problems.q: Which of these gases effuse faster than O2 (31.998 g/mol)? He is 4.0026, Ne is 20.180, N2 is 28.014, Ar is 39.948, and Cl2 is 70.90. Type the formulas of every gas that is faster.
problems.why: He, Ne, and N2 are lighter than O2, so they effuse faster. Ar and Cl2 are heavier.
hints: Keep every gas lighter than O2 at 31.998 g/mol. That leaves He, Ne, and N2.

nearMiss.hint: Ar is 39.948 g/mol, heavier than O2, so it is slower.
Cl2 is 70.90 g/mol, heavier than O2, so leave it off.
